_comment: The open design questions a carve-out can depend on. cluster.py tags a
declaration with a contingency when one of its rules matches, and a
cluster inherits the contingencies of the clusters it needs. The decision
numbers are the ones the api-graph lane was given; the decisions document
itself isn't in this repository, so each entry says in its own words what
the tool takes the question to be, and each rule is a concrete check.
A rule's weight scales the ranking penalty (1 = blocks outright); a rule with
inherit: false (a platform fact) doesn't pass to the clusters that need it.
Rule kinds: noncopyableType, hasDeinit, lifetime, declRegex, pathRegex,
referencesPath (any edge target, node or vocabulary), referencesNodePath
(new types only), module, platform, throwingClosure, changedThrows,

contingencies.title: Owned types
contingencies.question: How owned (noncopyable) resource types look: OwnedFD itself, adopting and giving up a raw value (init(taking:), relinquish()), consuming close, and what a deinit does with a close error (item 54, deliberately unresolved).
contingencies.deliberatelyOpen: Item 54, the close policy: OwnedFD's deinit drops close errors today. That's the default the package ships, not a decision; trapping on EBADF was tried in a2401b7 and reverted in 40e2dc8.

rules.evidence: {path} is noncopyable
{path} has a deinit, so it needs a close policy (item 54)
{path} uses OwnedFD
{path} consumes or borrows an owner

contingencies.title: Typed throws
contingencies.question: Plain wrappers throwing Errno are precedent on main (Stat, FileOperations, IORing), so they don't count. What's open is API that has to combine a caller's error with an Errno, as closeAfter does when both the body and close fail, and changes to an existing throws clause.

rules.evidence: {path} runs a throwing closure and throws itself, so the body's error and an Errno from cleanup have to be combined
{path} changes the throws clause of existing API
{path} throws a generic or non-Errno typed error

contingencies.title: Span and Lifetimes
contingencies.question: API that takes or returns span types, or depends on lifetime annotations (the experimental Lifetimes feature), whose shape and availability floors depend on the toolchain.

rules.evidence: {path} takes or returns a span
{path} has a lifetime annotation or is ~Escapable

contingencies.title: The sockets fold
contingencies.question: Whether SystemSockets stays a separate module or folds into SystemPackage. It decides the module a sockets pitch targets, and whether SystemSockets keeps its own copies of SystemPackage internals.

rules.evidence: {path} is in SystemSockets

contingencies.title: The Win32 namespace and platform enums
contingencies.question: Whether Windows keeps getting POSIX-shaped API through the UCRT (which Vision.md says has to die) or Windows-native API in a Win32 namespace (SYS-0010), and how multi-platform enums wrap each platform's owners. New API that compiles on Windows extends the UCRT layer; API for a concept that a Win32 draft also covers should share its name.

rules.evidence: {path} compiles on Windows, through the UCRT's POSIX layer
{path}: byte-range locking, which draft SYS-0014 covers for Win32
{path}: a descriptor's path, which draft SYS-0016 covers for Win32
{path}: file system information, which draft SYS-0015 covers for Win32

contingencies.title: PThread's deinit
contingencies.question: What destroying an unjoined PThread does: join (the package's default), detach, trap, or leak. Types nested in PThread need the PThread name to exist, but not this answer.
contingencies.deliberatelyOpen: Item 80: PThread's deinit joins, or detaches when it runs on the thread itself. That's a default to measure the others against, not a decision.

rules.evidence: {path} is the owned thread, whose deinit is the question

contingencies.title: Public errno
contingencies.question: Whether System makes errno (Errno.current) public. SystemSockets can't see SystemPackage's internal accessor, so it keeps a copy of it and of the helpers built on it.

rules.evidence: {path} reads errno through SystemSockets' own copy of Errno.current
{path} exposes errno in its signature

contingencies.title: The SE-0529 FilePath move
contingencies.question: If FilePath moves out of System, API that extends it or nests types in it becomes an extension of a type System doesn't own, and may need another home or spelling.

rules.evidence: {path} extends FilePath
{path} uses a type nested in FilePath

contingencies.title: Reaping an owned child process
contingencies.question: What an owned child process does when it's destroyed unreaped. The processes lane's work; nothing on system-next matches yet at the time of writing.
contingencies.deliberatelyOpen: Item 28: whatever default the implementation picks is not a decision.

rules.evidence: {path} wraps {cname}
{path} is an owned process type
